chunks: It is narrated from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about those witnesses whose testimony is rejected, so he said: “The suspected one, the accused one, and the adversary.”
He said: I said, “Then what about the immoral one and the dishonest one?” He said: “This falls under the suspected one.”

key_terms.ٱلشُّهُودِ: witnesses whose testimony is being evaluated
key_terms.ٱلظَّنِينُ: a person under suspicion whose reliability is doubted
key_terms.ٱلْخَائِنُ: a dishonest or treacherous person who betrays trust
key_terms.ٱلْخَصْمُ: an adversary or litigant in a dispute
key_terms.ٱلْفَاسِقُ: an openly immoral person lacking upright conduct
key_terms.ٱلْمُتَّهَمُ: a person accused or regarded with suspicion in the matter

ai.seo_question: Whose testimony is rejected in Islamic legal proceedings according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding the rejection of testimony in judicial matters. It identifies the suspected person, the accused person, and the adversarial party as unacceptable witnesses, and clarifies that the immoral and dishonest are included under the category of the suspected.
